summary: The bill exempts defined less-than-lethal projectile devices from federal firearms restrictions under title 18, excise taxes under the Internal Revenue Code, and National Firearms Act requirements by amending the relevant definitions and establishing 90-day Attorney General or Treasury classification processes plus annual technology reviews.

scores.thoughts: The bill contains no provisions related to government spending, appropriations, or budgets. It focuses exclusively on regulatory exemptions and tax changes for certain devices.

Title II explicitly exempts less-than-lethal projectile devices from the firearms and ammunition excise tax under IRC Section 4181 and from National Firearms Act provisions. This constitutes a targeted tax reduction for these items.
No provisions address healthcare, insurance, medical services, or public health programs.

Title I amends 18 U.S.C. § 921 to exempt defined less-than-lethal projectile devices from federal firearms restrictions. Title II further removes them from NFA oversight. This reduces regulatory barriers and expands legal access to these devices, aligning with protecting gun rights.
No content relates to immigration, borders, visas, or enforcement.
No provisions touch on reproductive rights, abortion access, or related regulations.
The bill does not address military budgets, defense procurement, or armed forces policy.
No environmental, regulatory, or climate-related measures are present.
No welfare, entitlement, or social assistance programs are mentioned.
The legislation has no bearing on schools, education funding, or school choice.
No references to controlled substances, decriminalization, or drug enforcement.

The bill's stated purpose involves law-enforcement de-escalation tools, but it achieves this solely through deregulation of devices rather than sentencing, policing, or rehabilitation reforms. The connection is too indirect for a nonzero score.
No trade, tariffs, or globalization provisions exist.
The bill does not address deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal policy beyond a narrow tax exemption.
No provisions relate to LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
Foreign aid, international assistance, and diplomacy are not addressed.
No election integrity, voting access, or electoral reform content.
The bill does not regulate technology companies, data privacy, or surveillance.
No labor, union, or employment provisions are included.
Religious exemptions and anti-discrimination rules are not mentioned.
